blocks.text: Spunweb Nonwoven Ltd converts polypropylene (PP) granules into spunbond nonwoven fabric rolls and sells them business-to-business to converters that make diapers, sanitary pads, surgical disposables, carry bags, crop covers and similar products [F] (AR2026 p.130) [F] (CALL May 2026). It makes money on the spread between the fabric price per kg and the PP and masterbatch cost per kg: raw materials consumed were Rs 232.4 cr against revenue of Rs 324.5 cr in FY26, about 72% of sales [E] (AR2026 p.127). The group runs seven Chinese-built lines with 39,140 MTPA of installed capacity, all in Wankaner, Gujarat, split between the listed parent (SNL, 20,400 MTPA, 3 lines) and its wholly owned subsidiary Spunweb India Pvt Ltd (SIPL, 18,740 MTPA, 4 lines) [F] (PPT May 2026) [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Sales are on monthly or at most quarterly purchase orders, with no long-term supply contracts [MC] (CALL May 2026). The mix figures above come from a 'management information report', not audited notes, and the audited accounts report a single segment [F] (AR2026 p.157).

Listing status: shares were listed on the NSE Emerge SME platform on 21 July 2025 after a Rs 60.98 cr fresh-issue IPO at Rs 96 per share [F] (AR2026 p.35) [F] (AR2026 p.36). Our earlier internal notes said this was a mainboard listing; that is wrong, and the annual report confirms SME status [F] (AR2026 p.67) [F] (BOARD). In practice this means half-yearly rather than quarterly results, exemption from Regulations 17-27 of the listing rules (no corporate governance report), 972 shareholders and almost no institutional ownership [F] (AR2026 p.43) [F] (NUMBERS). The prospectus was not available to us, so IPO objects, pre-IPO restated history and lock-in schedules cannot be checked.

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: theses 1 and 2 are company-specific (ramp-up and operating leverage); thesis 3 is company-specific and one-off (a step change in cost, not a recurring growth driver); thesis 4 is structural; thesis 5 is company-specific and one-off (IPO money); thesis 6 depends on the earnings cycle; thesis 7 is structural to the order pattern of a fragmented converter base.

items: 1. Cash conversion is poor. CFO was Rs 3 cr against PAT of Rs 23 cr in FY26 and Rs 3 cr against Rs 11 cr in FY25, so CFO/PAT was 0.41x over three years and FCF was negative Rs 31 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Reported profit is going into inventory and receivables [AI].

2. Headline growth is inflated by the acquisition. Our statements data show 43% FY26 sales growth and a 40.8% 3-year CAGR [F] (NUMBERS), but FY25 consolidates SIPL only from 27 December 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.34). Proforma group growth was 22.2% [MC] (PPT May 2026), and the parent alone grew 16.5% [F] (AR2026 p.34). The DCF's 30% starting growth rests on the inflated series [F] (NUMBERS).

3. Working capital is getting worse. The cash conversion cycle went from 59 days in FY24 to 123 in FY25 and 136 in FY26, with inventory days at 114 [F] (NUMBERS). Raw-material stock rose 75% to Rs 44.7 cr [E] (AR2026 p.147), and receivables older than one year rose from Rs 0.6 cr to Rs 2.5 cr [E] (AR2026 p.148).

4. The product is commodity-like with no contracts. PP spunbond on Chinese lines is a capacity-driven product, orders are monthly POs, and management concedes there are no long-term contracts [MC] (CALL May 2026). Implied realisation per tonne fell about 8% in FY26 [E] (PPT May 2026).

5. Raw-material exposure is large. Material is about 72% of sales and 52% of it was imported in FY26, up from 43% [F] (AR2026 p.157). A 10% input-cost shock that is not passed through would cut FY26 EBITDA by about 41% [E]. Pass-through is a management claim that has not been tested through a full PP cycle [MC] (CALL May 2026).

6. Group structure built through related-party deals. SIPL was a promoter partnership acquired in FY25: the company paid the two promoters Rs 8.48 cr in cash for SIPL shares while issuing them equity worth Rs 8.49 cr [F] (AR2026 p.159). The parent also sold Rs 39.6 cr of goods to SIPL in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.47).

7. Disclosure is thin and inconsistent. Three different export numbers (Rs 54.2 cr, Rs 44.3 cr and 10.61% of sales) appear, segment mix differs between the deck and the call, the key audit matter section is blank, and the FY25 balance-sheet comparative does not total [F] (AR2026 p.150) [F] (AR2026 p.156) [F] (AR2026 p.126) [MC] (PPT May 2026).
8. Everything is at one site in Wankaner, Gujarat, and every line was sourced from China [F] (PPT May 2026) [MC] (CALL May 2026).
9. Liquidity is thin on the SME platform. There are 972 shareholders, FII holding fell from 0.87% to 0.05%, and the price is 41% below the 52-week high [F] (NUMBERS).

10. The bear DCF shows how much the equity depends on margin. At a 10% EBITDA margin the bear case gives Rs 16 per share, 83.5% below the price, because Rs 77 cr of debt absorbs most of the enterprise value [F] (NUMBERS).

Is the growth 43% or 22%? The market screens 43% growth and a 10x P/E [F] (NUMBERS). On a like-for-like group basis growth was 22% [MC] (PPT May 2026). The market may be over-reading the growth; equally, a 10x P/E on 22% growth is not demanding [AI].

Is the margin structural? FY26 EBITDA margin of 17.25% includes a FY24-FY26 run of PP pass-through, and the second half (16.91%) was below the first (17.73%) [MC] (PPT May 2026). The base DCF already assumes a fall to 14% [F] (NUMBERS). If the margin holds near 17%, the DCF understates value; if PP volatility bites, the bear case matters [AI].

Is the working-capital build a one-off? Management attributes it to new hygiene customers starting on 90-day credit, SKU stocking and raw-material buying [MC] (CALL May 2026). If FY27 CFO stays near zero, it is structural [AI].

Packaging lines and mix: the new lines serve packaging at margins 1-1.5 pp below hygiene [MC] (CALL May 2026). As they ramp, blended margin may fall, which runs against the 'slightly higher margin' guidance [AI].

Undiscovered or unloved? The stock trades at the IPO price (Rs 97 against Rs 96) after a Rs 165 high [F] (NUMBERS) [F] (AR2026 p.35). That could reflect neglect of an SME stock, or a correct discount for poor cash conversion [AI].

blocks.text: Our variant view [AI]: the market is right about the price but often for the wrong reason. On reported numbers the stock looks like a 10x P/E compounder at 43% growth with 27% ROCE [F] (NUMBERS). On cleaner numbers it is a 22%-growth commodity converter whose profits are being reinvested in working capital rather than turning into cash [MC] (PPT May 2026) [F] (NUMBERS). The reverse DCF needs 14.6% five-year sales growth at a 14% margin [F] (NUMBERS). That is below proforma growth and below the volume headroom from Lines 6 and 7, so the price is not demanding on growth. What it does require is that working capital stops absorbing all the profit. The swing factor to watch is the cash-flow statement, not the P&L.

subsections.title: How recent the current business is

blocks.text: [AI] The listed group in its current form is about 15 months old. SIPL, which carries 48% of capacity and contributed 31% of FY26 consolidated profit, entered the group in December 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.160) [F] (PPT May 2026). Lines 6 and 7 were commissioned around January 2026, and the board, committees, CFO and CS date from late 2024 [MC] (CALL May 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.38). Our statements data before FY25 describe only the parent, so the five-year history is not like-for-like [F] (NUMBERS) [F] (AR2026 p.34). The operating know-how is older (a family business since 2007), but the listed group, its governance and its consolidated numbers have about one clean full year behind them [MC] (AR2026 p.18).

items: 1. Procurement: PP granules and masterbatches, about 52% imported (Singapore and Saudi Arabia are mentioned) and about 48% domestic, partly under one-year MOUs with Reliance and IOCL [F] (AR2026 p.157) [MC] (CALL May 2026).
2. Incoming quality control: MFI testing of resin [MC] (PPT May 2026).
3. Extrusion and spinning: granules are melted and extruded through spinnerets into continuous filaments; S, SS and SSS beams set the number of layers [MC] (AR2026 p.8).
4. Web formation and thermal bonding (calendering) into fabric of 7-150 GSM on lines 1.6, 2.6 or 3.2 m wide [MC] (AR2026 p.7).
5. Finishing: hydrophilic, UV, FR, anti-static or soft-touch treatment; lamination and sheet cutting (lamination line added around 2023) [MC] (PPT May 2026).
6. Lab testing (wetback, strike-through, hydrostatic head, tensile and others) and dispatch of rolls to converters [MC] (PPT May 2026).
7. Sale on monthly or quarterly POs; hygiene customers typically get 90-day credit [MC] (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: Value sits in a conversion spread of about Rs 31 per kg on FY26 numbers: revenue of about Rs 106/kg less material of about Rs 75/kg [E] (PPT May 2026) (AR2026 p.127). About Rs 18/kg of that reaches EBITDA [E]. [AI] The spread holds up in hygiene, where qualification on GSM uniformity and hydrophilicity creates some customer stickiness. It is thinner in packaging, where many local players run similar Chinese lines. Management's own margin gap between hygiene and packaging is only 1-1.5 pp of EBITDA [MC] (CALL May 2026), which suggests the hygiene premium is modest.

The business is moderately capital-intensive. Net fixed assets of Rs 78 cr support Rs 324 cr of sales, a fixed-asset turnover of 4.15x [F] (NUMBERS). It is working-capital-heavy: inventories plus receivables of Rs 153 cr are about twice net fixed assets [E] (AR2026 p.126). Management says it outsources production to other mills when a sector runs out of capacity, before committing to a new line [MC] (CALL May 2026). New lines take 12-18 months of OEM lead time and 12-18 months to ramp, and technical-textile capital subsidies (20% of capex, per management) require bank debt [MC] (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: The grade split covers only four of the six grades and sums to 99.5%, so FR and anti-static sales appear negligible or are included elsewhere [E] (PPT May 2026). Hydrophilic grades are only 2.45% of revenue even though hygiene is 51.94%, which suggests hygiene revenue is mostly super-soft and hydrophobic back-sheet fabric rather than specialised top sheets [AI] (PPT May 2026).

[AI] We treat packaging hydrophobic fabric (most of the 35.7% packaging revenue) as commodity-like: it is sold through traders who split rolls for bag makers, with seasonality now reduced by plastic bans [MC] (CALL May 2026). Hygiene super-soft and hydrophilic grades are semi-differentiated because they need customer qualification. UV agri covers and FR and anti-static grades are niches too small to move the numbers. Management has deferred value-added and laminated products, citing trade-war and Iran-war uncertainty [MC] (CALL May 2026). In the near term, then, the mix is shifting towards the commodity end as the packaging-dedicated Lines 6-7 ramp [AI].

Audited accounts report one segment, 'Non-Woven Fabric' [F] (AR2026 p.59) [F] (AR2026 p.157). subsections.title: Why segments moved and our read

items: Hygiene: management cites unused hygiene capacity being filled by onboarding new customers, BIS-driven import substitution of diapers and 11-month demand [MC] (CALL May 2026). Our read: plausible, but the new customers came on 90-day credit and SKU-specific stocking, so the growth cost working capital [AI].
Packaging: management cites plastic bans and year-round travel demand [MC] (CALL May 2026). Our read: this is where the 6,500 MTPA of new capacity goes, so packaging's share will rise in FY27 [AI].
Medical and agriculture: management names both as strategic entries in its outlook [MC] (AR2026 p.58). Our read: at 8% and 4% they are options, not drivers [AI].
Exports: management says US sales were paused because of tariff uncertainty and value-added export products deferred [MC] (CALL May 2026).

subsections.title: Strategy or mix, currency and trade policy

blocks.text: Management presents exports as opportunistic: it exports when export margins beat domestic ones and switches to India otherwise. US business was paused during the tariff uncertainty, and value-added export products were deferred because of the 'trade war' and the Iran war [MC] (CALL May 2026). The top export markets are Oman, Nepal, UAE, USA and Saudi Arabia [MC] (PPT May 2026). Currency exposure is net short USD: FY26 foreign-exchange outgo was Rs 144.0 cr (raw-material imports Rs 127.0 cr CIF and capital goods Rs 16.2 cr) against foreign-exchange earnings of Rs 44.3 cr [F] (AR2026 p.54) [F] (AR2026 p.156). Hedging policy is not disclosed. Unhedged foreign-currency exposure is not disclosed. Specific tariff dates are not given in the documents [AI].

Both entities, all seven lines and the solar plants are in Wankaner, Rajkot/Morbi district, Gujarat [F] (AR2026 p.7). Any local disruption (power, flood, labour or regulatory) would hit 100% of capacity [AI]. Insurance expense was Rs 0.32 cr [F] (AR2026 p.153). The adequacy of insurance cover is not disclosed.
